findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is I/O (console logging) fused inside the parsing/transform pipeline of load_metrics, which violates Data/Calculations/Actions: the shell must own all logging while the core is pure.
findings.failure_mode: Pure logic has observable side effects; the function cannot be unit-tested without capturing stdout, and logging leaks into the calculation layer.
findings.fix: Remove the println! from load_metrics entirely. If logging is needed, push it to the caller/shell layer after domain construction, or return a log message as part of a typed result.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file-not-found, permission-denied, or I/O error. Absolute laws forbid unwrap in production.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted filesystem input causes process abort instead of returning a typed, recoverable error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)), and propagate to the caller.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range value strings. Absolute laws forbid unwrap in production.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data aborts the process instead of yielding a typed parse error.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing. A line with zero fields or only one field will panic.
findings.failure_mode: Short or empty lines cause IndexOutOfBounds panic instead of a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to extract name and value, eliminating indexing entirely.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast: any u32 > 65535 silently truncates to u16.
findings.failure_mode: Out-of-range values silently wrap, corrupting the domain model with invalid values.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) instead of as u16, returning a typed overflow error.

findings.problem: load_metrics accepts raw &str path and raw primitive fields, parses them inline, and constructs Record directly — raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: The domain type Record is built from unvalidated String and numeric fragments; no parse boundary enforces invariants before data enters the core.
findings.fix: Define a ParseBoundary function that takes raw CSV lines, returns Result<Record, ParseError> using split_once and fallible constructors. Record construction should only succeed from validated values.

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging (println!), allocation, and domain Record construction into a single function. This violates the mandatory Data/Calculations/Actions architecture.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot reason about purity of the core; cannot test parsing in isolation; shell effects are mixed with calculation logic; violates Holzman invariant-density and parse-boundary laws.
findings.fix: Split into: (1) a pure parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for calculation, and (2) a shell function that reads the file, maps parse_line with .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?, and optionally logs. Keep I/O and logging separate from parsing.

findings.problem: All errors (I/O, parse, overflow, underflow, invalid format) collapse to panic via unwrap. There is no typed error enum.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from numeric overflow; no recovery or retry logic is possible.
findings.fix: Define an enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid, Overflow } and use map_err throughout to return typed errors.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() builds an intermediate Vec<String> for every line. SKILL.md mandates split_once for one-separator grammars and avoiding intermediate materialization.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary per-line heap allocation; split_once would avoid Vec entirely for the two-field case.
findings.fix: Replace with line.split_once(',').map(|(name, val)| Record { name: name.trim().to_string(), value: ... }) and eliminate the intermediate Vec and collect.
